reason: The cited evidence (E1) only discusses CrN coatings on stainless steel and a CoCrNiSi0.3 medium-entropy alloy, noting benefits for wear and corrosion resistance up to 550 °C. It provides no data or discussion on boride-based materials, molten aluminum corrosion, or the specific high-temperature diffusion barrier mechanism against aluminum. Thus, the key premise that this protection transfers to boride components in molten aluminum is entirely unsupported.
premises: CrN coatings deposited by reactive sputtering are dense and stable at high temperatures.
CrN coatings act as a diffusion barrier against corrosive media.
The protective behavior of CrN on stainless steels and related alloys is transferable to boride-based components.
